title: 27th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:03 with 32 members present and was the last sitting of the second session of 2025. The Speaker announced committee changes and sent the President's Human Rights Commission nominations to the Human Rights and Gender Committee, while the South Galolhu member's privilege motion over the Foreign Minister's earlier reply failed to win a vote to be debated (8 yes, 37 no). Two bills had their first readings, a Maldives Media and Broadcasting Regulation Bill and a Re-employment Bill, and members then began the preliminary debate on the media bill: supporters stressed accountability and committee-stage fixes, while opponents said it would restrict journalists. The Speaker closed the debate for the day so members could study the bill, then summed up the session's work and closed the sitting at 10:13.

items.title: Praises and prayers; opening of the sitting
Attendance of members
items.outcome: 32 present, 6 on leave, 4 on official travel

items.title: Announcements from the chair (changes to committee membership)
items.outcome: Hithadhoo Central member Ahmed Azaan Marzooq named to the Security Services Committee in place of the Vilimale' member and to the Finance Committee in place of the North Henveyru member

items.title: President's letter nominating three people for the Human Rights Commission of the Maldives
items.outcome: letter read out; sent to the Human Rights and Gender Committee for review

items.title: Privilege motion (Rule 208) by the South Galolhu member over the Foreign Minister's reply to a question in the 13 August sitting
items.outcome: vote to allow debate failed 8-37 (45 voting, 23 needed); no debate held

items.title: Maldives Media and Broadcasting Regulation Bill (sponsor Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru, Thulhaadhoo)
Re-employment Bill (government bill, sponsor Hanan Mohamed Rasheed, Guraidhoo; title partly garbled in the text)
Preliminary debate on the Maldives Media and Broadcasting Regulation Bill
items.outcome: ten members spoke; chair ended the debate for the day so members could study the bill, with no vote

items.title: Closing remarks on the second session and close of the sitting
items.outcome: Speaker summarised the session's work; sitting closed at 10:13

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Moved a privilege matter, saying the Foreign Minister's answer about a photo of a person in an 'India Out' T-shirt misled the Majlis.
Opposed the media bill, arguing it is a government-driven effort, backed by PNC members, to restrict media and journalists.
In points of order, replied that the MDP has voted for many bills, disputing claims that it opposes every bill.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Thanked the sponsor and said the MDP opposes every law the PNC brings, including laws on gangs, drugs and tax.
Said media must be regulated and answerable, citing false reports about children and individuals, and criticised past press access under the MDP government.
Supported the bill fully and said any problems can be fixed at committee stage.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said the government has cut the powers of the Majlis, the courts and judges, and described the bill as an attempt to put the media behind it.
Said a government cannot be run by locking down media or jailing journalists, and urged the bill's withdrawal or rejection.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Raised points of order that the bill was submitted by an individual member, yet PNC and government members were being blamed for it.
Said bills submitted by members should be accepted and debated, including those submitted by the South Galolhu member.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Opposed the bill, saying it aims to strip the media of its rights and is in effect a government bill brought through the Thulhaadhoo member.
Said media must remain free to report on theft and corruption, and that members would not be intimidated into dropping the issue.

speakers.name: Ahmed Saleem
positions: Said the media is the fourth estate and must report facts without harming people's honour, drawing on Islamic teachings.
Said officials must also answer questions truthfully, and that members should set an example in how they speak in the chamber.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Presented the bill to replace the Media Council and Broadcasting Commission with one regulator of seven members, four chosen through media outlets.
Said it aims to protect press freedom, set ethical codes and discipline, and curb false news, citing the Constitution and Islamic teaching.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Raised a point of order objecting to remarks that described members as 'bots', calling it improper language about members.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Noted an earlier similar bill was withdrawn and said the present text draws on media laws in the EU, UK, Ireland and Singapore.
Said the commission's majority would come from the media itself, so concerns can be raised at committee stage, and that media should be accountable.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill, saying journalists' concerns can be addressed at committee stage and that one merged commission suits the country's budget.
Stressed protecting people's honour from false reports, citing Islamic teaching.

decisions: Committee changes announced: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq (Hithadhoo Central) joins the Security Services and Finance committees.
The President's Human Rights Commission nominations were sent to the Human Rights and Gender Committee for review.
The South Galolhu member's privilege motion was not accepted for debate (8 yes, 37 no).
First readings were announced for the Media and Broadcasting Regulation Bill and the Re-employment Bill.
The chair ended the preliminary debate on the media bill for the day so members could study it further.
The Speaker closed the sitting, the last of the second session, at 10:13.
